newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends firm, above lows on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends firm, above lows on fund buying.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures staged a dramatic turnaround, ending higher and well above their early lows on fund-related buying, traders said.

KCBT wheat was broadly lower early on spillover pressure from CBOT corn and soybeans, which were weak after beneficial rains fell Saturday over dry growing regions of Illinois. Meteorologists said more rain was in the forecast Monday through Wednesday.
KCBT September wheat set an intraday low in fast, early dealings at $3.41, down 8-1/2 cents.
But fund-related buying of CBOT and KCBT wheat surfaced at the midsession and propelled the market above its lows.

Wheat also drew support from poor growing conditions in other wheat-growing areas of the globe. Specifically, traders cited heavy rain in central Europe that could cause serious harvest delays, and dry conditions in wheat-growing regions of Australia.

"Even though we look set to have a good (wheat) crop here in North America, carry-out levels are still relatively low and therefore weather in other countries is still a big factor," a KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat settled 3-1/2 to 6-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with Sept up 3-1/2 cents at $3.47-1/2.

Traders said Rosenthal Collins was the featured buyer in both KCBT and CBOT wheat pits, picking up at least 4.5 million bushels of KCBT Sept wheat. Chicago sources said Rosenthal bought about four million CBOT Sept.
E. D. & F. Man International bought 2.5 million Sept and sold one million Sept. Farmers Commodities sold two million Sept.
